reason: The cited evidence shows that WC addition improves wear resistance in a similar HEA system (E1, E2), but none of the passages involve TC4 substrates, laser cladding on titanium alloys, or demonstrate that the substrate's bulk properties are preserved. The specific claim of successful application to TC4 is unsupported.
premises: Adding WC particles to a CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA matrix increases hardness and wear resistance compared to the HEA alone.
Laser cladding can produce a dense, metallurgically bonded HEA/WC composite coating.
The HEA/WC composite coating will bond well to a TC4 substrate without degrading its beneficial properties.
The wear mechanism of the HEA/WC coating is primarily abrasive, with reduced spalling and cracking.
